scope: Final strict named-flower, robot-hand, contact, and temporal acceptance for real flower-arranging frames 182-270
summary: A 48-pixel exact contact-protection band plus the strong trained-policy repair passed all 39 unchanged gates after independent GPU SAM2 re-tracking, making this second large-motion window eligible for full-film expansion.
evidence: strict-object-gate-v6/gate-report.json records 39/39 passing gates, WORKING, and ALLOW_FULL_FILM_EXPANSION.
Aligned motion preservation is 0.841027, target identity is 0.979992, and temporal consistency is 0.774540.
Upper-hand-to-cream contact has p90 7.289 and maximum 9.487 pixels; lower-hand-to-lime contact has p90 7.358 and maximum 9.434 pixels, passing the unchanged 8/15-pixel thresholds.
Both hands and both unambiguous named flowers are nonempty in all 89 frames after independent post-repair tracking on physical A800 GPUs 4 and 5.
The accepted lossless candidate has SHA-256 1ff0da6efa99a587c4c258e5f546aa5b53e3709e55d4b1e4562dfa826270c9e9.
lessons: A sufficiently wide exact interaction band can protect thin stems and gripper contact while allowing temporal repair elsewhere in the character region.
Selecting the first policy round that passes compatibility is safer than maximizing the temporal score, but this window needed the strong round because the less aggressive rounds remained below 0.75.
limitations: Exact identity is claimed for the cream and lime flowers; the visually retained pink flower remains excluded because of ambiguous correspondence during rapid rotation.
Contact remains a 2-D camera-pixel measurement and the result covers one 89-frame overlap window.
next_actions: Freeze this window, retake remaining human-failure windows with source-face suppression, and apply the same independent tracking/contact/temporal gate before stitching.
